label: Surplus AI
summary: Private, offline AI system for ASU Surplus, in production. Built on the job from June 2026; processing per item dropped from about 15 min to about 3 min.
metrics: ~80% less processing time per item, about 15 min down to about 3 min; ~10 min to list a 100+ unit pallet, instead of 1 to 2 hours; 14B Qwen model across four Mac minis, offline, via MLX
skills: MLX, Flask, Bash, Apple Vision OCR, Qwen 14B, Llama 3B, local LLM serving
text: Private, offline AI system for ASU Surplus Built on the job, in production Surplus staff were typing hardware specs into a spreadsheet by hand, which introduced typos into the inventory. Writing product listings was also manual. One connected pipeline: collect specs, build a master spreadsheet, and have AI write the listings, all on a private network that never touches the internet. Handles identification, condition grading, pricing, label printing, and database export. Runs offline: Qwen 14B across four Mac minis plus Llama 3B on one, via MLX. Replies stream word by word. Merge rules keyed on serial number, so a low-quality read never overwrites good data. Traced repeated cluster failures to macOS permissions and network routing. A Listings tab builds a strict prompt from each row’s real specs, and a Cluster tab polls each node over SSH every 5 seconds. Five-node cluster. Five M1 Mac minis on a gigabit switch with no internet uplink, fixed IPs, and passwordless SSH from the head node. Apple’s MLX framework splits one model across several machines with tensor parallelism, so a 14B model can run across Macs that can’t hold it individually. USB spec collector. A Bash script on a USB stick runs system_profiler on each Mac, reads model, chip, RAM, storage, battery health, and macOS version, looks up year and screen size from a reference table, and de-duplicates by serial number. Camera inventory scanner. For Macs that won’t boot, a webcam photographs the bottom label and Apple’s Vision OCR reads the model number, EMC, and serial. These are matched against the lookup table to get product, year, screen size, and resale lane (Retail, Auction, or Parts). Merge logic. Both sources land in one master inventory keyed on serial number, so a camera scan never overwrites real data from a working machine. Surplus AI app. A Flask server runs two model engines: Qwen 14B across four nodes, and Llama 3B on one node for quick responses. Replies stream word by word. A Listings tab builds a strict prompt from each row’s real specs, and a Cluster tab polls each node over SSH every 5 seconds. Launchers. One double-click starts everything, waits for the engines to respond, and opens the app. Closing it shuts down every node.

label: Autonomous Supply Chain Watchtower

text: Multi-agent LLM system Personal project, built solo Turning raw sales history into a logistics plan normally takes several manual steps by different people. Three agents running in sequence on the native Anthropic Claude API through CrewAI, each consuming the previous agent’s output.
